A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Synthio study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across moves.

before.justification: v1 reports original audio-classification experiments across ten datasets, audio-captioning results, and supplementary generation-quality and ablation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and adds filtering, generator-configuration, and combined-augmentation experiments in Tables 11–14.

M1.justification: The proposed DPO alignment, MixCap prompting, CLAP filtering, self-reflection, and classifier-training pipeline remain unchanged. v2 adds pseudocode and clarifies CLAP fine-tuning and the existing captioning adaptation; these disclosures do not establish a changed method. Alternative generators are tested as ablations.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten classification datasets and AudioCaps captioning/generation tasks. Sound-VECaps and AudioCaps already appear as training data in v1. The added studies vary configurations within existing coverage; the new few-/zero-shot discussion introduces no corresponding evaluation.

E2.justification: The principal baseline sets in Tables 1–10 remain unchanged. v2 adds comparison variants, including Synthio without CLAP, Synthio with Tango, Synthio trained using AudioCaps, and Synthio combined with traditional augmentations. Tango previously appeared in generator-quality comparisons, but the classification comparison in Table 13 is new.

E3.justification: The principal splits, metrics, and training budgets are retained. Added experiments introduce CLAP thresholds of 0.3, 0.5, and 0.85, alternative generator configurations, and augmentation combinations. Section 6.3 changes the stated exclusion from the captioning generator's training data from AudioSet to AudioCaps; unchanged Table 4 results do not establish that this experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Tables 11–14 substantially extend diagnostic evidence: they test whether CLAP filtering helps, sensitivity to its threshold, dependence on generator architecture and training data, and compatibility with traditional augmentations. Figure 5 also replaces the environmental-sound portion of the long-tail analysis with additional NSynth categories. The earlier diversity, synthetic-only, scaling, and FAD analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged across three runs. v2 adds no seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical tests, including for its new experiments.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises many FSD50K entries: Synthio changes from 15.41 to 13.91 at n=50 and from 24.93 to 23.89 at n=500. DCASE Gold-only at n=500 changes from 36.68 to 34.30. Tables 11–14 add substantial new results, and Figure 5 revises class-specific findings. The PDFs do not explain the revisions to retained-setting scores.

T1.justification: The DPO and diffusion mathematics in Equations 1–17 are retained. Changes to variance-schedule notation and relocation of background explanations introduce no new assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, and conclusion retain the same central claims about consistent and diverse synthetic augmentation, ten-dataset evaluation, and the stated 0.1%–39% advantage. Shortened contribution bullets do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: The appendix adds explanations linking diminishing augmentation gains to the diversity of real data, interprets CLAP filtering as protection against occasional LLM hallucinations, and discusses training-data dependence and complementarity with traditional augmentation. The principal limitations concerning generator quality, LLM bias, and computational cost remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies two DPO losers per instance, CLAP threshold 0.85, text guidance scale 7.0, last-layer CLAP fine-tuning, and n=100 for the scaling experiment. It also clarifies the captioning adaptation and adds Algorithm 1. The stated code/checkpoint status changes from promised release after acceptance to availability on the project page.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a few-/zero-shot audio-classification discussion and positions synthetic augmentation as complementary. Additional references include work by Feng, Xu, and several few-shot researchers; the appendix adds comparisons with Azizi's findings. The central positioning around synthetic augmentation and diffusion alignment is retained.

P1.justification: v2 condenses contribution and methodology passages, moves some diffusion background into the appendix, and adds appendix subsections and an acknowledgment. Author notes and publication headers change. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The appendix gains four experimental tables and a standalone algorithm display. Figure 5 is redrawn as an NSynth-only chart with changed categories and axis ticks. Existing figures and tables are largely retained, with resizing and relocation accompanying the expanded appendix.

improvement.justification: v2 fills concrete implementation gaps and adds useful tests of filtering, generator dependence, and augmentation compatibility. Its AudioCaps-exclusion statement also resolves v1's inconsistent captioning-training description. These gains are limited by new reporting problems: Tables 11–12 give TUT accuracy at n=100 as 71.23, versus 52.42 in Table 1, and some revised Figure 5 annotations disagree with bar heights. The added documentation and diagnostic evidence support a limited overall improvement, without establishing substantially stronger reliability.
